# Story 21 — CI pipeline: GitHub Actions runs the suite on every push (Story: CRM-28)

## Prerequisites

- **PLATFORM-11-WEB** must be shipped first. The web suite this workflow runs is the one that story creates (test setup, `vitest run`, jsdom + Node 26 `localStorage` shim). CI cannot report on a suite that does not exist.
- Thirteen platform plans already sit in `.squad/plans/platform/`; this is the fourteenth. Corrected in review — the generated text claimed it was the first (L-21).
- No `.github/` directory exists in the repository — this story creates it. Confirm before you start with `ls .github` returning "No such file or directory".
- **Coordinate:** the branch-protection rule on `main` is set in the GitHub repository's **Settings → Branches**, needs an admin, and cannot be committed. This story leaves that step to a human and names it explicitly under **Done Criteria**.

---

## Story Goal

Every push to the remote runs the three suites — the API test suite, the web test suite plus the web production build, and the four repo-level check scripts — from one GitHub Actions workflow. A failing suite blocks the merge (through a branch-protection rule set in the GitHub UI, not in the workflow file). Each suite reports its own duration, a hung test is killed by a per-test timeout and reports itself, and every step runs even when an earlier step went red so one push tells the whole story.

**Not in scope:** structure checks (owned by PLATFORM-15-ALL), deployment, Android, coverage thresholds, linting, formatting, changes to any existing test / check script / `package.json` script.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** no CI runs. A push reveals nothing until a reviewer pulls the branch and runs the suites by hand.
- **New behaviour:** every push and every pull request runs the API suite, the web suite, the web build, and the four repo-level check scripts. A failure in any step fails the run; the remaining steps still execute so a red push reports the full picture in one round trip. A pull request cannot be merged into `main` until all named checks are green (enforced by a GitHub branch-protection rule the person setting up the repository configures, not by the workflow file).

## Implementation tasks

### 1 — Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

**Create file:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

Contents (single file; no other workflow files, no reusable actions, no composite actions):

```yaml
name: ci

# Triggered on every push (every branch) and on every pull request into
# main. The pull_request trigger is the one branch protection binds to;
# the push trigger is what makes the branch's own history visible.
on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

# A push is a run; a run is not repeated for the same ref. This cancels
# an in-flight run of an older commit on the same branch so a fast
# follow-up push does not queue behind stale work.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Deliberately narrow. This workflow reads code, runs suites, and
# reports; it does not need write access to anything.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:

  api:
    # 20 minutes is a per-job kill switch. It is NOT the mechanism the
    # story asks for on hanging tests — that is per-test, below, on the
    # `npm test --` line. This job-level ceiling exists so a runner that
    # is truly wedged is eventually returned to the pool.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: api
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Pin to Node 26 explicitly. api/package.json declares `>=22.13`
      # (a floor, not a version the suite has ever been run on) and
      # node:sqlite's DatabaseSync — the only database access in the API
      # — is young enough that a different major is a different product.
      # Local development is on v26.3.1.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '26'
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: api/package-lock.json

      - name: install
        run: npm ci

      # `node --test` prints `duration_ms` for each test and a run
      # summary at the end. Passing `--test-timeout=30000` via `-- …`
      # sets a PER-TEST ceiling: a hung test is killed at 30s and
      # reported as a failing test, and the rest of the run continues.
      # The job-level `timeout-minutes` above would instead kill the
      # whole run and report nothing, which is what the story forbids.
      - name: api suite
        run: npm test -- --test-reporter=spec --test-timeout=30000

  web:
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: web
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '26'
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: web/package-lock.json

      - name: install
        run: npm ci

      # vitest prints its own per-file duration table and a total. The
      # `--testTimeout=30000` flag is the vitest equivalent of the API
      # per-test ceiling above.
      - name: web suite
        run: npm test -- --testTimeout=30000

      # L-15: a green web suite once sat on top of five type errors.
      # `npm run build` runs `tsc -b && vite build`; both must succeed.
      # `if: always()` runs this step even if the suite failed, so a
      # red push reports both failures in one round trip.
      - name: web build
        if: always()
        run: npm run build

  checks:
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # These scripts are plain Node with no imports outside the
      # standard library. `npm ci` is deliberately NOT run here — there
      # is no root package.json, and adding one is out of scope.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '26'

      # Each check runs even when an earlier one fails, so one push
      # reports every finding.
      - name: verify backlog
        run: node scripts/verify-backlog.mjs

      - name: verify taxonomy
        if: always()
        run: node scripts/verify-taxonomy.mjs

      - name: verify docs
        if: always()
        run: node scripts/verify-docs.mjs

      # verify-plan.mjs looks Jira keys up when .squad/secrets.yaml is
      # present and WARNS rather than failing when it is not. That file
      # is gitignored and does not exist in CI; every other check in
      # the script (ids, citations, dialect, statuses, casing,
      # duplicates, the heading number) runs without any credential.
      # The Atlassian token is intentionally not stored in GitHub
      # Actions secrets — see the story intake for the rationale.
      - name: verify plan
        if: always()
        run: node scripts/verify-plan.mjs
```

**Do not** add any other file under `.github/`. No `dependabot.yml`, no `CODEOWNERS`, no issue templates, no reusable workflows.

**Do not** create a root `package.json` to unify the two packages. `api/` and `web/` remain separate, each with its own lockfile, each installed with its own `npm ci`.

**Do not** add or edit `.gitignore` for `node_modules/` — each root already handles it (`web/.gitignore` is 37 bytes; `api/` has no untracked node_modules to worry about).

**Do not** add a step that greps commit messages for AI attribution: the API suite's `api/src/platform/http/no-ai-attribution.test.js` already covers the runtime surface, and history scrubbing is called out in `docs/git.md` lines 58–65 as a known deviation, not a CI check.

### 2 — Document the manual branch-protection step

**Create file:** `.github/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md`.

The file is prose only; it is not consumed by CI. It exists so the person configuring the repository has a single source for the exact check names to require. Write it as follows (concise, no marketing tone):

- State: this file records the branch-protection rule the story cannot commit. It is not machine-consumed. Delete it only when GitHub's rule is set and captured elsewhere.
- List: navigate to **Settings → Branches → Branch protection rules → Add rule** for `main`.
- Under **Require status checks to pass before merging**, mark **Require branches to be up to date before merging** and add these three checks by their job-name-based identifiers (the names GitHub displays after the first workflow run):
  - `ci / api`
  - `ci / web`
  - `ci / checks`
- Under **Restrict pushes that create matching branches**, ensure direct pushes to `main` are refused; `docs/git.md` line 12 already forbids them by convention, this makes it mechanical.
- Note: the branch-protection rule is not visible in the repository tree. A reviewer who wants to confirm it must open the repository settings. The workflow alone does not block a merge.

### 3 — No other file changes

- **No changes** to `api/package.json`, `web/package.json`, any test file, any check script, or `README.md`.
- **No changes** to `docs/git.md` line 22's reference to CRM-28 adding automated pruning — this story does not add branch pruning. If the reference needs updating, it is a separate story; note the mismatch under Edge Cases below.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **A hung API test.** The `--test-timeout=30000` flag passed via `npm test --` kills that one test at 30 seconds and marks it failed; the rest of the run continues and `node --test`'s final summary shows the failure with its duration. Enforced in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` under the `api` job's `api suite` step.
- **A hung web test.** vitest's `--testTimeout=30000` does the same for a single test in the web suite. Enforced under the `web` job's `web suite` step.
- **A wedged runner.** `timeout-minutes: 20` on each job returns the runner to the pool if the per-test ceilings themselves fail (for example, a `beforeAll` hook that spins). This is the second line of defence; the story's "reports itself rather than stopping the run" criterion is answered by the per-test flags.
- **First red step hides the second.** `if: always()` on every step after the first in each job (and on every check-script step in the `checks` job) forces the remaining steps to run. A red push reports the full picture in one round trip.
- **`.squad/secrets.yaml` is not present in CI.** By design. `scripts/verify-plan.mjs` lines 13–15 document that the Jira lookup warns rather than fails when the file is missing. Every other check the script does runs without a credential. Do not add the token to GitHub Actions secrets.
- **A pull request from a fork.** `pull_request` triggers run in a read-only, no-secrets context by default; the `permissions: contents: read` and the absence of any secret reference make this safe. Fork PRs run identical checks to internal branches.
- **`main` on macOS vs Linux casing.** Branch names are case-sensitive on Linux and case-insensitive on macOS (`docs/git.md` lines 25–28). The workflow runs on `ubuntu-latest`; a story branch pushed with the wrong-cased key will fail before checkout because the ref does not exist. Nothing here to fix — the runner behaves like the enforcement tier.
- **An intermittent test.** `node --test` and `vitest run` both print duration on every case. A test that occasionally passes stays visible because the summary and per-case durations are not suppressed by any reporter flag we add. Do not add `--test-reporter=dot` or vitest `--reporter=silent`.
- **`docs/git.md` line 22 promises CI adds branch pruning.** This story does not. Flag as a docs follow-up under a separate item; do not sneak it in here.
- **No `android/` build.** The story is `-ALL` in name but Android has no source. A Gradle job now would pass over an empty set; leave it to PLATFORM-18-MOB.

## Test Plan

This story adds no test files. Its acceptance is behavioural, observed on the runner:

1. **Push a branch with a passing tree** and confirm the Actions tab shows three jobs — `api`, `web`, `checks` — all green, with per-suite duration visible in each job's log.
2. **Push a branch that deliberately breaks one API test** (a `throw new Error('sink')` in a single test file) and confirm: the `api` job fails; the `web` job still runs and passes; the `checks` job still runs and passes. A pull request from that branch to `main` must show the failed check and (once the branch-protection rule is in place) refuse to merge.
3. **Push a branch that deliberately breaks one web test** and confirm the `web build` step still runs after the failing `web suite` step (proof of `if: always()`).
4. **Push a branch that deliberately breaks the web build only** (a TypeScript error in `web/src/main.tsx`), while leaving `web test` green, and confirm the `web` job fails on `web build`. This is the L-15 case.
5. **Push a branch with a test that sleeps 60 seconds** and confirm the per-test timeout fails that test at ~30 seconds with a `duration_ms` around 30000 in the summary, and the rest of the run completes. Do **not** confuse this with the 20-minute job timeout, which would abort the run and report nothing.
6. **Revert each seeded failure** before merging the story.

No existing tests are modified. Do not add a workflow-lint step (`actionlint`, `yamllint`): coverage, linting, and formatting are all out of scope per the intake.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Migration:** first push after merging this story is the first run. There is no data to migrate; the workflow file lands and the runner picks it up.
- **Half-applied state:** if the workflow file lands but the branch-protection rule has not yet been created in the GitHub UI, merges are **not** blocked by red checks — the workflow reports, but nothing enforces. This is the reason the manual step is called out in **Done Criteria** and in `.github/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md`.
- **Rollback:** delete `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (and `.github/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md`); remove the branch-protection rule in the GitHub UI. No other state is left behind — no caches to purge, no secrets to revoke.

## Verification Steps

1. **Workflow syntax parses:** on the story branch, run `python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"` (yaml is standard-library-adjacent via PyYAML on most CI images; locally, use whatever YAML parser is on the machine). A parse error here is caught before the runner sees the file.
2. **API suite runs locally:** in `api/`, run `npm ci` then `npm test -- --test-timeout=30000`. Confirm the summary line prints `duration_ms` and the exit code is 0.
3. **Web suite and build run locally:** in `web/`, run `npm ci`, then `npm test -- --testTimeout=30000`, then `npm run build`. Confirm each prints a duration summary and exits 0.
4. **Check scripts run without install:** in the repository root, from a clean checkout with no `node_modules/`, run each of `node scripts/verify-backlog.mjs`, `node scripts/verify-taxonomy.mjs`, `node scripts/verify-docs.mjs`, `node scripts/verify-plan.mjs`. Each must exit 0 (or warn, in the case of `verify-plan.mjs` without `.squad/secrets.yaml`, per its comment at lines 13–15).
5. **No AI attribution anywhere in the new files:** run `` grep -rniE 'co-authored-by|generated by|claude|copilot|chatgpt|assistant' .github/ `` and confirm zero matches. This proves the workflow file itself carries no attribution, satisfying the standing rule the API suite enforces at runtime via `api/src/platform/http/no-ai-attribution.test.js`.
6. **Push to remote:** push the story branch to `git@github.com-azm:mazen-azm/crm` and confirm the Actions tab lists a run named `ci` with three jobs. Confirm each job's log ends with a duration line for its suite.
7. **Regression:** open a pull request into `main` from the story branch, seed a failing test as described under Test Plan step 2, and confirm the merge button shows the failed check.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists with the three jobs `api`, `web`, `checks`, each pinned to Node 26 and each caching its own lockfile.
- [ ] `.github/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md` exists and names the three required checks (`ci / api`, `ci / web`, `ci / checks`) with the exact GitHub Settings path to configure them.
- [ ] The API job runs `npm ci` then `npm test -- --test-reporter=spec --test-timeout=30000` in `api/`.
- [ ] The web job runs `npm ci`, then `npm test -- --testTimeout=30000`, then `npm run build` in `web/`. The build step carries `if: always()`.
- [ ] The checks job runs the four `scripts/verify-*.mjs` files under Node 26 with no `npm install`. Each verify step after the first carries `if: always()`.
- [ ] Every job sets `timeout-minutes` (job-level kill switch) and every test run passes a per-test timeout flag (`--test-timeout` / `--testTimeout`). The plan and the file comments say plainly which does what.
- [ ] `.squad/secrets.yaml` is **not** referenced anywhere in the workflow. No Atlassian token is added to GitHub Actions secrets.
- [ ] No changes were made to `api/package.json`, `web/package.json`, any test file, or any check script.
- [ ] A push with a green tree produces three green jobs; a push with one red step still runs the remaining steps in the same job (proven by seeding a failure and observing the log).
- [ ] A pull-request run appears in the Actions tab for a PR into `main`.
- [ ] **Manual, cannot be committed:** a repository admin has created a branch-protection rule on `main` requiring `ci / api`, `ci / web` and `ci / checks`. Until this box is ticked in the GitHub UI, "a red suite blocks a merge" is only half true; the plan says so plainly.
- [ ] `grep -rniE 'co-authored-by|generated by|claude|copilot|chatgpt|assistant' .github/` returns zero matches.
